source.title: V-FIND: Revealing the Intrinsic Forgery Knowledge Encoded in Video Forgery Detectors
source.authors: Shi-Chao Kan; Chengpeng Hong; Jing-Tong Dou; Chuan-Cheng Shi; Yuhan Liu; Linrui Xu; Yi-Xiong Liang; Yi-Gang Cen; Yan-Peng Sun; Fei Shen; T. Chua

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether sparse, functionally specialized neurons carry video-forgery-discriminative information in video detectors, a new setting relative to the claim's language-model and InceptionV1 examples.
record.gate_note: The study measures selected-neuron subspace performance against fixed-budget controls and intervenes on selected neurons, reporting task-specific detection effects. It does not test any version's stated model, proportion of neurons with named jobs, explanation fidelity, or attribution-graph claim. Prior-work baseline results quoted in the paper are not recorded. The PCA values in Figure 7 are not included because the text does not state their exact numbers.
record.test_reason: The study uses the idea of sparse, task-specialized neurons as a tool. It selects 211 forgery-discriminative units in a frozen Qwen2.5-ViT video detector and reports its own method's detection performance and intervention effects. It does not audit what share of neurons have one job, does not examine canonical polysemantic neurons, does not compare interpretability across tools or architectures, does not build attribution graphs, and does not score neuron explanations. The reader's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own finding that every version is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that forgery-discriminative knowledge is concentrated in a sparse set of functionally specialized neurons, and that video forgery detectors hold sparse, extractable, reusable forensic knowledge, with interventions showing these neurons' functional specificity.
record.recipe_differences: The study localizes layers using real–fake representation discrepancies, selects units using probe-based effect sizes, and tests them with a frozen-backbone linear readout and activation swaps; it does not use the claim's neuron-explanation or pole-counting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports performance changes with feature budget, selection threshold, layer interval, discovery-set size, and input frame count; these are task-performance sensitivities, not measures of named-job interpretability.

fits_no_version.finding: In the Qwen2.5-ViT video forgery detector, 211 effect-size-selected units from layers 28–30 beat same-budget random units as a linear-readout subspace (Magic mACC 89.37 vs 83.04). Swapping their activations shifts decision logits more than same-layer random swaps (+0.884 vs +0.414 in Fake→Real).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-discriminative signal in a vision-transformer forgery detector is concentrated in a small set of late-layer units whose activations causally affect the decision more than matched random units.

record.problems: The direct neuron-intervention evidence is reported for the Qwen2.5-ViT detector and a video-forgery task; it does not establish that neurons have one human-nameable job or provide a share of interpretable neurons. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded PCA's fixed-budget values from Figure 7 because their exact numbers are not stated in the text. Also excluded the paper's broader benchmark, robustness, and training-data results because they do not directly test selected-neuron specificity or intervention effects.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or of job-count shares.
No language models and no interpretable-share measurement across scale or across dense vs MoE models.
No analysis of InceptionV1 or of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No measurement of interpretable-neuron share against tools, architecture or regularization.
No attribution graphs and no comparison with a replacement model.
No test of explanations from activating examples against where neurons fire.

record.verdict_notes: 'Functionally specialized' here means discriminative for a binary real/fake task, chosen by probe-weighted effect size. It is not an interpretability judgement that units have one human-nameable job, so the study gives no evidence on the share of clean neurons. No uncertainty is reported anywhere. The cross-architecture results (Table 3) are also method performance and bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B or count neuron poles by number of jobs or by understood status.
Does not test language models, dense versus mixture-of-experts models, or scale up to trillions of parameters.
Does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models or test whether better explanation tools or architecture raise such shares.
Does not build attribution graphs or test their reconstruction of behavior against a replacement model.
Does not test explanations against activating examples or measure whether they predict where a neuron fires.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating their activations on new text.
